item.title: Former WTVM anchor arrested in Minneapolis church protest
item.description: A former reporter at WTVM in Columbus, Ga., which covers multiple east Alabama counties, was one of the people arrested in the Minneapolis church protest, according to the television station.Georgia Fort, now working as an independent journalist, live-streamed the moments federal agents arrived at her home to take her into custody. item.title: ‘There’s a lot of garbage in the appropriation bills we voted on’: Tuberville votes to pass government funding package despite concerns
item.description: U.S. Sen. Tommy Tuberville (R-Auburn) voted to pass a package of government funding bills on Friday to avert another major government shutdown.According to POLITICO, the package of appropriations bills would fund operations for multiple federal agencies through the remainder of the fiscal year, plus fund the Department of Homeland Security for two weeks to give lawmakers more time to negotiate possible changes to ICE sought by Democrats. item.title: Ex-boyfriend fires into bonfire gathering, Rainbow City Police say
item.description: The Rainbow City Police Department announced the arrest of two people in connection with a bonfire shooting on Monday.Anthony Paul, 19, of Hokes Bluff, and a juvenile were arrested.Police responded to shots fired in the area of Friendship Road at 8 p.m. A group of people at the location reported that they were gathered around the fire when a vehicle repeatedly drove past the location. item.title: Massive search underway for suspect in Randolph, Cleburne Counties
item.description: Multiple agencies are searching for a person of interest in a death investigation in east Alabama.The search operation is focused on the north end of Randolph County and the south end of Cleburne County.Danny Lee Carter has been on the run since Tuesday after a male victim was found dead in the Cool Springs area.The search began around County Road 10 but has expanded to include County Roads 47, 25 and 10. item.title: Sean of the South: It is a sin to kill a mockingbird
item.description: It’s raining hard. Thundering loudly. Like the world is falling apart. And yet there is a mockingbird outside my window.The bird is unfazed by the downpour.Funny. I’ve never seen a bird in the rain before. Admittedly, I don’t know anything about birds. But I thought most birds, except waterfowl, found shelter during rainstorms.I move closer to get a better look. item.title: Reviving rural Alabama: How Southern hospitality is offering renewed momentum in Monroeville
item.description: MONROEVILLE — Along the Alabama River lies a history lesson in economics. In the days of the steamboat, towns and communities sprouted along the river, and families settled to make a living wage in the cotton and corn industries.Today, much has changed due to technology, an ever-evolving transportation system and foreign policies that put hardworking Americans out of work. item.title: House Dems, led by Juandalynn Givan, bristle at Democrat-sponsored bill to protect children from secondhand marijuana
item.description: MONTGOMERY — Thursday, on the floor of the Alabama State House, State Rep. Patrick Sellers (D-Pleasant Grove) stood firm in support of his legislation to protect children from the harmful effects of secondhand marijuana smoke even as members of his own party spoke against it. The bill passed the House with 77 in favor, two against and 18 abstentions. item.description: State Rep. item.description: In a heavyweight bout that showcased the two winningest SEC programs over the last nine seasons, Auburn’s four-game winning streak came to an end as Tennessee led for all 40 minutes on Saturday night in Thompson-Boling Arena en route to a 77-69 victory. With the loss, Auburn dropped to 14-8 overall and 5-4 in league play.
